data.title: Trump, Milei under pressure to explain Bolsonaro flight from Brazil
data.description: BRASíLIA - US President Donald Trump and Argentina's Javier Milei faced mounting pressure Friday to explain the role their countries played in helping Flavio Bolsonaro flee Brazil after he had his passports cancelled.

data.title: Polish riot police deployed after court chief suspended
data.description: WARSAW - Riot police deployed around Poland's constitutional court and President Karol Nawrocki called off an African visit on Friday after the suspension of its chief justice in a battle between the centrist government and the nationalist right.

data.title: France fears new street violence at Halloween protests
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Shops and businesses in Paris and other French cities on Friday boarded up windows amid fears of fresh street violence during a third consecutive weekend of protests -- this time clashing with Halloween.

data.title: British king reflects on colonial atrocities in Guyana
data.description: GEORGETOWN (GUYANA) - Britain's King Charles paid homage to fallen soldiers and reflected on colonial atrocities in Guyana during a whistle-stop tour of the former colony on Friday.

data.title: Monaco taken off global money-laundering 'grey list'
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Global anti-money laundering watchdog the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) said Friday it had removed Monaco and three other countries from its "grey list", two years after it put the principality among its territories requiring increased monitoring.

data.title: Scottish police probe Andrew, Epstein stay at royal castle: UK media
data.description: LONDON - Scottish police are in the "very early stage" of probing the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's reported stay at the royal Balmoral estate at the invitation of ex-prince Andrew, UK media reported Friday.

data.title: Tears, fear, anger: relatives of Spain train crash dead await fate
data.description: TOLEDO (SPAIN) - Marisa Liebana could barely hold back her tears as she sought news about her nephew Francisco Jose, one of the 69 victims of this week's high-speed rail crash in Spain.

data.title: UN nature talks in extra time as nations struggle to reach deal
data.description: YEREVAN - The UN biodiversity summit spilled into overtime Friday, pushing negotiations into the night as nations wrangled over how to get a landmark deal to halt nature's destruction back on track.

data.title: Thousands of students, workers hold peaceful protests in Italy
data.description: ROME - Thousands of students and workers took to the streets across Italy on Friday, calling for more school funding and relief from the soaring cost of living, in massive protests that remained mostly peaceful.

data.title: Vatican says Pope Leo voted in US midterm election
data.description: ROME - Pope Leo XIV, the first US-born leader of the Roman Catholic Church, has voted in the United States midterm elections, submitting his mail-in ballot in Chicago, the Vatican said on Friday.

data.title: US jury backs Bayer in weedkiller cancer case
data.description: A US jury has sided with the multinational company Bayer over three women’s claims its Roundup weedkiller caused their cancer, the latest blow to plaintiffs in thousands of similar cases.

data.title: 'Horrific' Russian drone strike kills 13 at Ukraine train station
data.description: KYIV — A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine's Dnipro on Thursday killing at least 13 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a "horrific" attack that demands a response from Kyiv's allies.

data.title: Oil majors reap bumper profits as Mideast war drives prices
data.description: LONDON - Oil and gas giants Shell and TotalEnergies on Thursday reported soaring quarterly net profits as the Middle East war pushed up hydrocarbon prices -- and the cost of living around the world.

data.title: Rains bring relief to haze-weary Indonesian city
data.description: PALANGKARAYA, Indonesia - Residents and firefighters in an Indonesian city long shrouded in a toxic haze brought on by months of wildfires rushed outside dancing and chanting as rain this week brought a welcome respite.

data.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
data.description: JERUSALEM — Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc on Thursday piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that made strong gains after an otherwise indecisive election.

data.title: Falklands War munitions fashioned into ‘Chalice of Peace’ for the pope
data.description: BUENOS AIRES - Combining the remnants of shell casings and other items from the Falklands War, Argentine silversmith Juan Carlos Pallarols is crafting a "Chalice of Peace" to give to Pope Leo XIV when he visits Argentina next month.

data.title: ‘My blood was spilled here’: Tanzania election violence not forgotten
data.description: DAR ES SALAAM - A year after Tanzania’s bloody election, many remain traumatised by the violence, while government critics live in fear of abduction and arbitrary arrest, or facing treason and terrorism charges.

data.title: EU and Canada to open ‘new chapter’ at Montreal summit
data.description: MONTREAL, Quebec - Canada and the European Union will craft “a new chapter” in their alliance at a summit that opens on Thursday, the EU chief said, as they navigate uncertain relations with the United States.

data.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles into East Sea
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea fired short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast on Thursday, Seoul’s defence ministry said, less than a week after South Korea proposed talks over a growing border row.

data.title: Trump’s border: quiet, but few people are happy
data.description: SAN LUIS, Arizona - Between the hundreds of migrants arriving every day to seek asylum, chases of those fleeing, and the encounters with drug traffickers, Jason Mercado was overwhelmed during his time working for the US Border Patrol under Joe Biden.

data.title: Afghanistan opium poppy cultivation surges despite ban
data.description: KABUL - Opium poppy cultivation in Afghanistan more than quadrupled in 2026 despite a Taliban government ban, the United Nations said Thursday, urging that impoverished farmers needed alternatives to the lucrative crop.

data.title: Cuba wins UN vote against US embargo but support dips
data.description: UNITED NATIONS - The UN General Assembly on Wednesday adopted a new resolution calling for an end to the US embargo against Cuba, although support for the communist-ruled island fell to its lowest level in three decades.

data.title: Cuba wins UN vote against US embargo with weakest backing in 30 years
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - The UN General Assembly on Wednesday adopted a new resolution calling for an end to the US embargo against Cuba, although support for the communist-ruled island fell to its lowest level in three decades.

data.title: Putin hails Elon Musk as 'truly a genius'
data.description: MOSCOW - US tech tycoon Elon Musk is "truly a genius" for deploying thousands of satellites into orbit, President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday, as Moscow seeks to develop its own satellite internet network.

data.title: Italian PM slams 'shameful' release of alleged protest organiser
data.description: ROME - Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Wednesday slammed a "shameful" decision by a judge dismissing accusations against a campaigner arrested on terrorism charges for allegedly seeking to organise violent protests.

data.title: Bolsonaro's escape to the US: How it happened
data.description: SAO PAULO - Flavio Bolsonaro's clandestine escape to the United States bewildered Brazil and triggered a frantic search for his whereabouts.

data.title: World Bank warns of worsening food insecurity as commodity prices soar
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The World Bank on Wednesday warned that global commodity prices were set to increase by 23 percent by the end of 2026, with energy prices at four-year highs due to the war on Iran and food prices driven up by global conflicts and El Nino.

data.title: Clean-up starts as Serbian students movement prepares to govern
data.description: BELGRADE - Belgrade residents on Wednesday washed away politically charged graffiti that had stained city walls over months of protests, as Serbia's student-led movement prepared to govern after its seismic election victory.

data.title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 64
data.description: URDA, Spain - A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 64 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said after one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century.

data.title: Bolsonaro flees Brazil for US after election defeat
data.description: OPA-LOCKA, Florida - Brazil’s defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro arrived in Florida by private plane on Wednesday, after defying a court order that banned him from leaving his country.

data.title: Russell Brand gives evidence in rape trial
data.description: LONDON - British comedian and actor Russell Brand told his rape trial on Wednesday that he believed consent was “fundamental” to sexual relations, as he gave evidence for the first time.

data.title: Russia woos African leaders at Moscow summit
data.description: MOSCOW - A summit with nearly two dozen African leaders opened in Moscow Wednesday, with the Kremlin describing their countries as “natural allies” against the West.

data.title: Climate talks ‘a bunch of baloney and BS’, says Panama
data.description: YEREVAN, Armenia - Despite campaigning to host the next COP nature summit, Panama’s Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro has a blunt view of the UN-led negotiations he says are little more than “hypocrisy contests”.

data.title: Turkey brokers Libyan reunification talks
data.description: ISTANBUL - Turkey hosted talks between Libya’s eastern and western administrations last week with an ultimate goal of reunifying them, but no agreement has emerged, a senior Turkish official familiar with the talks told AFP Wednesday.

data.title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 30
data.description: URDA, Spain - A collision between two high-speed trains south of Madrid killed 30 people on Wednesday and the toll could rise, regional authorities said in Spain’s second such disaster this year.

data.title: Israel’s low-key president holds keys to next government
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israeli President Isaac Herzog is known for his unassuming and mild manner, but all eyes will soon be on him as he decides who to task with forming the next coalition government.

data.title: ‘Eat the rich’: Indonesians fed up with graft, wildfires
data.description: JAKARTA - Hundreds of Indonesians gathered in central Jakarta on Wednesday to protest against economic hardship, graft and the government’s handling of devastating wildfires causing toxic haze that has sickened thousands.

data.title: Flavio Bolsonaro on way to Ecuador after fleeing Brazil
data.description: BUENOS AIRES - Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro was on his way to Ecuador after fleeing Brazil, Argentina’s government said on Wednesday.

data.title: 3 arrested in Japan with rare tortoises from Thailand
data.description: OSAKA — A high school student and two men have been arrested on suspicion of attempting to smuggle rare tortoises and other animals from Thailand in violation of the Customs Act, police said on Wednesday.
